Jesus healed a man who had waited thirty-eight years by a pool.
And the man went straight to the authorities, and told them who did it.
John, chapter five.
Jerusalem. By the sheep gate, a pool called Bethesda.
Having five porches.
Under them lay a great multitude. Blind, lame, withered. All waiting for the water to move.
The King James says why. An angel troubled the water, and the first one in was healed.
But the oldest manuscripts don't have that verse.
Now, one man had been lying there thirty-eight years.
Jesus saw him, and asked a strange question.
Wilt thou be made whole?
Why ask that?
Because the man never says yes.
Sir, I have no man, when the water is troubled, to put me into the pool. While I am coming, another steppeth down before me.
Thirty-eight years, and no one to carry him four steps.
Jesus doesn't touch him. He doesn't use the pool.
Rise! Take up thy bed, and walk!
And immediately, the man was made whole.
But it was the Sabbath.
The leaders stopped him. It is not lawful for thee to carry thy bed!
He didn't even know who had healed him.
Later Jesus found him in the temple. Sin no more, lest a worse thing come unto thee.
And the man went, and told them it was Jesus.
Gratitude? Or betrayal? John doesn't say. But from that day, they sought to kill him.
In the eighteen-eighties, beside the Church of Saint Anne, they dug it up. Two great pools, with a wall between them.
Four sides, and one across the middle. Five porches.
And the question is still there. Wilt thou be made whole?
